subject: Horseshoe crabs
hook: HORSESHOE CRABS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Horseshoe crabs are not actually crabs or crustaceans, but are instead chelicerates more closely related to spiders, ticks, and scorpions.
angle_support: Despite their name, they are not crabs or even crustaceans; they are chelicerates, more closely related to arachnids like spiders, ticks, and scorpions.
Horseshoe crabs resemble crustaceans but belong to a separate subphylum of the arthropods, Chelicerata.
title: Why Horseshoe Crabs Are Actually Ocean Spiders
description: Horseshoe crabs look like prehistoric armored crustaceans, but their taxonomy tells a completely different story. Discover why their anatomy and appendages place them closer to scorpions and spiders than true crabs.
narration: HORSESHOE CRABS IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You spot an armored shell crawling along coastal sand and picture a standard crustacean. A genuine crab. But that name is a complete biological deception. They are not true crabs at all, nor are they crustaceans. Their lineage separated into a completely different subphylum over four hundred million years ago. Horseshoe crabs belong to Chelicerata. Beneath their horseshoe-shaped cephalothorax, they carry six pairs of appendages, including delicate mouth pincers known as chelicerae. This anatomical blueprint does not match crabs. Instead, it ties them directly to arachnids like scorpions, ticks, and spiders, as well as extinct giant sea scorpions. Virtually unchanged since the Triassic, they remain ancient arachnid relatives disguised in heavy armor. Flip that heavy marine shell over, and you are really facing a prehistoric cousin of the spider.
